collection.description: A howling wind comes up in the night, the kind that makes huts creak and babies cry.

ask.text:
A howling wind comes up in the night, the kind that makes huts creak and babies cry. In the morning, (name) walks out to the grain shelter and stops dead.
Half the thatch is gone. Just gone, torn off and scattered across the jungle. And the seed and grain from inside are scattered across the village like sand: on the paths, in the cooking area, in people's hair.
And every bird on the island seems to have heard the news. They are arriving in flocks. They look very pleased. (Name) doesn't know where to start. What should (he/she) do first?

choices.label: Check on the Granary Keeper's Family
Watch Which Way the Wind Tears

c1o1.text: Quick work saves the grain that landed on the swept floors of the huts and the clean stones of the cooking area. It goes back into the stores as usable food, and somehow, in the sweeping, a few forgotten baskets from the back of the shelter turn up as well. The birds leave, disappointed.

c1o2.text: Then the rain follows the wind. Before the roof can be covered, a whole basket of stored grain is soaked, swells up and starts to sprout, and must be thrown out. The birds, at least, are delighted.

c1.text: (Name) grabs a broom and shouts for help. Half the village turns out with brooms, baskets and very loud voices for scaring birds...

c2o1.text: Everyone is fine, just shaken. The keeper's family move in with neighbours until the roof is fixed, bringing their sleeping mats and a lot of grain in their hair.

c2o2.text: Seeing the last of the thatch about to go, (name) climbs up to tie it down while the wind is still gusting, and a loose roof pole swings round and strikes (him/her) hard across the shoulder. (He/She) falls, and is carried to the healers, and will need care for some days.

c2.text: (Name)'s family sleeps in the hut beside the granary. (He/She) runs to check on them first...

c3o1.text: (Name) notices the wind always rips the thatch from the sea side first, peeling it back like a banana skin. Talking to the builders, (he/she) realizes the other huts nearest the sea have the same worn edges. It's a useful pattern, and the builders start tying the sea-facing edges down twice as tight.

c3o2.text: (Name)'s notes and the builders' memories disagree about which side went first, and nobody can prove it either way. They decide to wait for more evidence before changing anything. The birds, meanwhile, keep eating.

c3.text: Before anyone fixes anything, (name) walks slowly around the granary, studying exactly how the roof came apart...

c4o1.text: The workers rethatch the granary roof before nightfall, tighter and thicker than before. When the wind comes back the next night, the roof doesn't even rustle. The birds give up and leave.

c4o2.text: Halfway through, the village runs out of rope. A passing trader has plenty, but wants grain for it. Some stored grain is traded away, leaving less food in the stores, but the roof gets finished, and finished properly.

c4.text: (Name) organizes a work crew, and they start on the roof straight away, while the birds watch hopefully from the trees...
